comments.content: In mark_plant_dead, death_date, death_reason, death_comment are bare parameters (not wrapped in Form(...) or a Pydantic model with Body). FastAPI will bind them as query parameters for this PATCH endpoint. This mismatches typical REST PATCH body usage, can cause encoding issues for multi-word reasons/comments, exposes data in URLs/logs, and will break clients expecting to send them in the request body (as form or JSON). Use Form or define a request schema.
comments.suggestion_code:
from fastapi import Form

async def mark_plant_dead(
    plant_id: str,
    death_date: str = Form(...),
    death_reason: str = Form(...),
    death_comment: str = Form(""),
    uow: SqlAlchemyUnitOfWork = Depends(get_uow),
):

comments.content: All new/modified endpoint functions lack explicit return type annotations (e.g. -> PlantListResponse). Per PEP 484 and project guidelines, public API functions should have full type hints for better IDE support, static analysis and maintainability. response_model= helps runtime but explicit -> is still recommended.

Docstrings for endpoints are minimal (one-liners). For public API routes, use fuller docstrings (e.g. Google style) describing parameters, return values, errors and filtering logic to improve maintainability.

comments.content: Manual construction of query strings in PATCH requests (with inline ? and & params, including manual + for space in death_comment) is error-prone and hard to maintain. Special characters in values (e.g. spaces, &, =) could break the URL. Use the test client's params= kwarg instead for automatic encoding.

Tests heavily rely on hardcoded values (exact counts like 2, specific plant IDs 'TO-2026-001'/'PE-2026-001', exact dates/reasons/comments, and is_dead flags). This makes them brittle to changes in underlying test data setup. Consider adding more general assertions (e.g. verify all returned plants match filter) or using parametrization for robustness.

comments.content: Uses loose equality '==' in validation (prohibited per code quality rules; must use '==='). Existing code in file uses strict '!== undefined && !== null' checks.

Hardcoded business URL paths '/api/plants', '/api/plants/${plantId}' and '/api/plants/${plantId}/dead' in URL builder functions. This is prohibited; should use centralized base URL or config to avoid maintenance issues if API prefix changes. (Note: similar hardcoding exists in prior code, but new additions continue the pattern.)

comments.content: Duplicate boilerplate: identical fetch + body extraction + JSON.parse + return pattern duplicated across the 3 new functions (and pre-existing functions). Consider extracting a shared request helper for future maintainability.

getListPlantsApiPlantsGetUrl conditionally appends query params only when truthy: `if (aliveOnly) ... if (deadOnly)`. False/undefined treated identically (no param sent). Combined with backend defaults, may cause incorrect filtering when explicit false values passed to listPlants(aliveOnly=false, ...).

mark_dead lacks type hints on parameters (args, db) and return. Only minimal one-line docstring. Public function violates PEP 484 and review guidelines requiring type hints + docstrings (Google/NumPy style) for all public functions.

comments.content: Death date validation only checks YYYY-MM-DD format via strptime; no range validation (e.g., must be after planting_date, not in future). Could persist invalid data like death before planting. Also, both --alive-only and --dead-only accepted without mutual exclusion (if/elif silently prefers alive_only).

The alive_only and dead_only parameters are not mutually exclusive. If both are True, the if-elif will only filter for alive plants (ignoring dead_only). This can lead to silent incorrect results. Add explicit validation, e.g. if alive_only and dead_only: raise ValueError('Cannot filter by both alive and dead').

Hardcoded magic strings 'dead'/'alive' and 'Other' used for status/reasons instead of constants (e.g. from PlantDomain). Reduces maintainability if DEATH_REASONS or status logic changes. Also, death details in show_plant added only to service branch; fallbacks (legacy db, markdown) do not display death info.

comments.content: Validation logic for death_date, death_reason, and death_comment is duplicated: inline checks are added inside create_from_dict (from_dict in diff) and a separate validate_death_fields static method. This duplication risks inconsistency if rules change. Consider extracting a single validation method and calling it from both __post_init__ and create_from_dict (or better, use __post_init__ for all and have create_from_dict just prepare data).

Death fields are public mutable attributes (death_date: str = "", etc.) with no @property setters for re-validation. __post_init__ only runs at construction time. Direct assignment like p.death_date = "bad-format" or p.death_reason = "Foo" after creation will bypass all validation and can corrupt is_dead property or lead to invalid state propagating downstream.
